page: Microsoft Azure HB368-288rs_v5 is a high-performance computing virtual machine instance built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by a dedicated x86_64 Intel processor, the instance allocates 288 dedicated virtual central processing units alongside 448.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.56 GB of memory per core. The architecture does not integrate hardware graphic accelerators.

For local disk operations, the instance features 15,875 GB of high-speed local NVMe solid-state storage. Furthermore, it supports Premium Storage and includes Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) networking capabilities designed for low-latency node-to-node communication in clustered deployments. It does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Hardware resource allocation establishes a compute-dense profile characterized by a lean memory-to-vCPU ratio. This profile suits highly parallel computation where execution is bounded by central processor density and direct high-throughput local disk caching rather than high per-thread memory capacity.

Microsoft Azure HB368-288rs_v5 is targeted at large-scale high-performance computing, computational fluid dynamics, engineering simulations, and parallel processing workloads requiring massive core counts, rapid local scratch disk throughput, and low-latency cluster networking.
